issues.title: [New Model]: Hy-Memory-30B-A3B on Atlas 300I Duo (310P) - validated with benchmarks
issues.body:
## Proposal

Add support/validation for Tencent Hunyuan's **Hy-Memory-30B-A3B** on **Atlas 300I Duo (310P3)**.

Hy-Memory-30B-A3B is a ~3B-active-parameter long-term-memory **writer** model (native `HYV3ForCausalLM`, already implemented in vLLM core — no custom code / `trust_remote_code` needed). It executes the write path of external memory frameworks (Mem0, MemOS, Hy-Memory, EverMemOS): given a conversation it emits structured memory entries as JSON. The Hunyuan family is currently tracked in the support matrix as `Hy3-preview 🔴 (A3)` / `Hy4-preview 🔵 (A3)`; this adds a 310P-validated data point for the A3B-class memory-writer derivative.

Docs PR: #19313 (tutorial + 300I Duo support matrix row).

## Model / Hardware

- Model: `Tencent-Hunyuan/Hy-Memory-30B-A3B` (Apache-2.0, ~60 GB BF16 checkpoint, 51 shards)
- Architecture: 48 layers, hidden 2048, GQA 32Q/4KV (head_dim 128, QK-Norm), 128 routed experts top-8 + 1 shared expert (expert intermediate 768), sigmoid routing + correction bias + route-norm × 2.826, first layer dense, vocab 120832
- Hardware: Atlas 300I Duo (310P3), FP16 (`--dtype float16`; 310P has no BF16, weights are cast on load)
- Weights (~60 GB) exceed a single chip's 44 GB HBM → **TP≥2 mandatory**. One 300I Duo card carries two chips, so TP=2 fits on a single card (HCCS); cross-card TP=2 also works (PCIe).

## Serving

```
vllm serve /model --served-model-name hymem --dtype float16 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 4096 --enforce-eager
```

> ⚠️ **Version requirement**: validated on `v0.27.1rc1-310p`. On `v0.26.0rc2-310p` the server starts and text stays fluent, but output degrades to echoing the user input or looping on `<think></think>` — the first-token distribution is still healthy (correct answer in top-2), the routed experts just don't contribute correctly. Between 0.26 and 0.27 the `hy_v3` model code switched from `FusedMoE` to `FusedMoEFactory`, which resolves the 310P MoE implementation selection. If you are stuck on 0.26, this model will silently misbehave.

## Validation (vLLM Ascend v0.27.1rc1-310p, FP16, TP=2, enforce-eager, greedy)

| Check | Result |
|-------|--------|
| Memory-extraction workflow (model card example, `reasoning_effort=no_think`) | ✅ exact JSON, all 3 memories extracted |
| zh/en chat ("你好，请用一句话介绍你自己。" → "我是混元，是由腾讯开发的大模型。") | ✅ |
| Math reasoning (9.11 vs 9.8 with explanation) | ✅ |
| TP=2 single card (2 chips, HCCS) vs two cards (PCIe) | ✅ both work |

| Metric | TP=2, single card (HCCS) | TP=2, two cards (PCIe) |
|--------|--------------------------|------------------------|
| Decode, batch=1 (256 tok) | 4.6 tok/s | 4.6 tok/s |
| Decode, batch=8 (256 tok each) | 31.9 tok/s aggregate | - |
| Prefill (1227-token prompt) | ~678 tok/s | - |

Decode is HBM-bandwidth bound (~3B active params across 128 experts per token), so chip interconnect (HCCS vs PCIe) does not change decode throughput; cross-card placement remains fully usable.

## Follow-ups

- W8A8 quantization on 310P (works for Qwen3-30B-A3B on this card) is the most promising decode speed-up, untested here
- ACL graph modes (piecewise/fullgraph) untested with `--enforce-eager`

Add community validation results and documentation for serving **Tencent Hunyuan's Hy-Memory-30B-A3B** (memory-writer MoE model, `HYV3ForCausalLM`) on **Atlas 300I Duo (310P3)**, following the WeMM-Embedding / EmbeddingGemma2 contribution pattern.

- `docs/source/user_guide/support_matrix/supported_models.md`: one row in the *Atlas 300I DUO* generative table

## Validation (310P3, FP16, vLLM Ascend v0.27.1rc1-310p, TP=2 `--enforce-eager`)

| Metric | TP=2, single card (2 chips, HCCS) | TP=2, two cards (PCIe) |

| Decode, batch=1 (256 tok) | 4.6 tok/s | 4.6 tok/s |

- The docs-only diff is based on current `main` for `supported_models.md` (the fork branch base predates some matrix churn; the file content in this branch is upstream-latest plus the new row, so the effective diff is the single added row).

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Pad incomplete 64-token KDA prefill chunks with neutral updates and trim padded outputs, fixing incorrect and nondeterministic tails. Pack each input once using the existing chunk metadata; a single-sequence output is trimmed with a view.

Refs #15665. Release counterpart: #19041.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Corrects partial-chunk prefill outputs, adding at most 63 neutral positions per affected sequence. Aligned inputs retain the existing path.

### How was this patch tested?

- CPU contracts, dispatch and state regression: 56 passed. Current-head pre-commit and both CPU UT CI jobs passed.
- The identical KDA implementation was validated with the release counterpart: captured 581-token native replay reduces last-five-token relative RMS error from 57.3% to 0.26% against an independent FP64 reference.
- 384 timed NPU wrapper calls: optimized outputs and final states match the previous padding fix bit for bit. At 131071 tokens, median latency improves from 12.04 ms to 10.90 ms; four ragged sequences improve from 7.21 ms to 6.36 ms. These are single-layer measurements.
- Release-branch `vllm bench serve` validation: 27 runs / 108 successful requests with 128K inputs. With an 8192-token scheduling budget, target/draft decode graphs and MTP5, median input throughput for output=1 differs by less than 0.2% from the previous padding fix. These results validate the shared implementation; they are not a separate full-model run of this main branch.
- Fresh full DeepSWE regression remains pending (draft).

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c4df37dfcc7f72ca41cd43801a468526ecf99a2b

issues.title: [Feature]: TurboQuant INT4 KV cache for DeepSeek-V4.1 (C1A/C2A layers)
issues.body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

**Ask:** make `--kv-cache-dtype turboquant_4bit_nc` usable on DeepSeek-V4.1 on A2/A3 — or, if V4.1 is intentionally out of scope, get the v0.30.0 release notes/docs corrected so the claim stops sending users down this path.

#### Why now: the shipped release notes claim this already works

The v0.30.0 release notes ("Hardware and Operator Support") list:

| Model | Hardware supported in this release | Release scope |
|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek V4.1 | Atlas 800I A3, Atlas 800I A2 | W8A8 serving; Model Runner V2 execution, **TurboQuant INT4 KV cache**, torch.compile, P/D deployment |

The DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash tutorial also documents the A2 two-node colocated recipe. Following the release claim, `--kv-cache-dtype turboquant_4bit_nc` is rejected at startup:

```
ValueError: Ascend turboquant_4bit_nc currently requires DeepSeek V4
```

Note that #18608 already proposes removing the DeepSeek V4.1 attribution and is still open, so 0.30.0 artifacts still advertise it.

#### Reproduction

- Image: `quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.30.0` (same behaviour on `v0.30.0rc2`), HDK 26.1.1, CANN 9.2.x
- Hardware: 2 × Atlas 800I A2 (8 × 910B3), DP2 / TP8 / EP16, `--max-model-len 1048576`
- Model: `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` W8A8 (`Eco-Tech/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-w8a8`; the official `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` config behaves the same)
- `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`, `--kv-cache-dtype turboquant_4bit_nc`, `--attention-config.indexer_kv_dtype int8`

#### Why it fails — three layers, not one

1. **Config gate** — `vllm_ascend/quantization/methods/kv_cache/turboquant/config.py:62`:
   `if hf is None or getattr(hf, "model_type", None) != "deepseek_v4": raise ValueError(...)`
   V4.1 declares `model_type="deepseek_v41"` / `text_config.model_type="deepseek_v41_text"` (verified on both checkpoints above), so the strict string comparison always fails.

2. **Path routing** — `model_uses_sfa_sparse()` returns False for V4.1 (it has `index_topk` *and* `compress_ratios`), so the DSA/compressed-cache validator above is the one that runs.

3. **Implementation is C4-only** — #17676 states the cache layout "only quantizes the memory-dominant C4 compressed KV state". `attention/dsa_v1.py` gates on `compress_ratio == 4` (line 1628) and has 17 TurboQuant references; `attention/dsa_v41.py` has **zero**, and `models/deepseek_v41/cache_config.py` builds only SWA/MLA/index specs. V4.1 `compress_ratios` are `0/1/2` → `SWA-only / C1A / C2A` (`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/sparse_mla.py:_V41_LAYER_TYPES`), i.e. **no C4 layer exists**.

Consequence: relaxing the model_type check alone would not produce a working TQ4 cache — it would either trip cache-spec/dtype validation or leave the cache in its existing dtype (the same silent "no effect" symptom seen with `fp8_ds_mla`).

For completeness, V4.1-Flash already satisfies every *numeric* constraint of the DSA validator: `head_dim=512`, `qk_rope_head_dim=64`, `index_topk=512`, 64 attention heads, bf16 weights, and the A2 profile exposes `TURBOQUANT_4BIT_NC_CACHE`. The `model_type` string is the only config-level blocker.

#### Questions

1. Is TurboQuant for V4.1 on the roadmap? If yes, is the intended target the C1A/C2A layers, and is the ops-nn `turbo_quant` kernel (plus `mixed_quant_sparse_flash_mla`) parameterized for non-C4 compression ratios and slot layouts?
2. Would a PR be reviewable that (a) relaxes the gate to `deepseek_v41*`, (b) adds a TQ page planner for C1/C2 layers, and (c) ports the `TurboQuantLatent` compress/inverse hooks into `dsa_v41.py`?
3. Is the Lloyd-Max codebook in `turboquant/latent.py` (trained on V4 latents, `legacy_hadamard=True`) reusable for V4.1 latents, or does it need recalibration?
4. If V4.1 is intentionally out of scope, can #18608 (or an equivalent) land so that the v0.30.0 release notes and docs no longer claim TurboQuant for V4.1?

### Alternatives

- Keep bf16 KV on V4.1 and recover capacity with Engram host offload (#16886) and/or KV Cache Pool.
- Use TurboQuant where it is supported today: DSA models with C4 layers (DeepSeek-V4-Flash) and SFA models (GLM-5.2/5.3).
- Relax the gate only, as an opt-in escape hatch, and document the risk — not recommended given the missing DSA-v41 cache path.

### Additional context

- Measured benefit on the supported model (#15821, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-W8A8, 1M in / 1K out, 90% shared prefix): ~1024 B → ~260 B per token (~3.94×), concurrency 4 → 10, 3910 → 5156 tok/s per card. On V4.1 only C1A/C2A layers would be eligible, so the gain would be smaller than V4's and should be sized before implementation.
- #18048 notes there is no TurboQuant e2e in CI (it needs a CANN with `cann_ops_nn.turbo_quant` and `key_quant_mode=3`); a V4.1 enablement would need an explicit accuracy/latency validation plan rather than relying on CI.
- Related: #18608 (attribution fix), #17676 (C4-only implementation), #15821 (original feature request), #19035 / #19036 (TQ + CP are mutually exclusive), #16886 (V4.1 1M OOM on A2, awaiting Engram offload).

issues.title: [Performance]: DeepSeek V4.1 bounded-replay tail ACL graph validation (PR #19286)
issues.body:
### Scope and existing implementation

This issue tracks the P-side bounded-replay prefill-tail graph path and the surrounding Host submission gaps in DeepSeek V4.1. **An implementation already exists in #19286: [Feature][Model] Support DeepSeek V4.1 decoder replay PIECEWISE ACL graphs.** Please use that PR as the implementation path rather than create a competing graph-support change.

At the time of this update, #19286 is open and unmerged, with head `ac329d46c7e721ed1a221c4d46a23d0e525c189c`. Its description reports a small accuracy smoke test and explicitly leaves final-head hardware/performance validation outstanding. This issue supplies profiling evidence and a focused performance-validation target for that work; it does not claim that the PR has already eliminated the measured gaps.

The requested scope is replay-tail ACL graph capture/replay in vLLM-Ascend. DSL/compiler optimization and QLI/QSLI/MQSMLA kernel changes are outside this issue. Bounded replay remains enabled; the comparison of interest is eager versus the supported graph path, not the benefit of switching bounded replay on or off.

### Observed environment

- Ascend 950DT, 28 AI Cores per device; two nodes, 8 devices per node.
- P and D each DP8 / TP1 / EP8; DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.
- vLLM: `4ba787ec9959e566d3b587a796dff07673324da5`.
- vLLM-Ascend: `6e3299ab492ddbadb4c8e3a00b88c982c9a28131`, local build.
- CANN 9.2.1, driver 25.6.rc3.1.
- The observed P configuration uses `enforce_eager=true`, graph mode `NONE`.
- The compared captures use the same metadata implementation: batch-local SWA group reuse plus equivalent request-offset simplification.

### Confirmed phase and profiling evidence

Workload: 128K input / 1K output, 90% shared prefix, concurrency 200, 800 requests. Both captures completed 800/800 requests. P was captured for 4.5 seconds and all eight ranks were parsed.

The affected GMM is under `vllm::dsv41_decoder_replay_forward → vllm::moe_forward_shared`, in P-side backbone prefill tail layers 20–39, **not DSpark draft decoding**. A representative `aclnnGroupedMatmulWeightNz_GroupedMatmul_GroupedMatmul` has activation shape 3605×5120 and device duration 367.838us. GMM1 → Swiglu → GMM2 is contiguous, with approximately 0.02–0.07us gaps; the large gaps surround that sequence.

- A representative full-device idle interval is 922.477us. The next backbone MQSMLA Host call lasts 945.070us and enters launch approximately 822us after call entry.
- Matching tail layers on the same rank shows approximately 0.9ms of MQSMLA Host preparation with replay both enabled and disabled. This Host work already exists; the shorter replay tail exposes it with less queued device work to overlap it. It is not a new 0.9ms operation introduced by bounded replay.
- Dynamic MoE work is also visible: `repeat_interleave → item → _local_scalar_dense` overlaps the first approximately 327us of a 786.432us idle interval. An aligned AllToAll instance has approximately 970us rank-arrival skew, already visible in Host submissions.

These measurements identify exposed Host work around the replay tail. They do not establish that all gaps are removable by graph replay. Dynamic synchronization and communication boundaries remain relevant.

### Graph integration and validation target

In the observed source, `make_decoder_replay` accepts `NONE` and `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`; other graph modes are rejected with `replay prefill requires eager execution; use NONE or FULL_DECODE_ONLY`. The replay custom op runs outside Dynamo and resolves mutable rows/context at runtime. Outside Dynamo does not itself mean outside every ACL graph: its documentation describes ordinary tail operators remaining in a captured graph, with nested attention capture boundaries.

#19286 directly addresses this integration: independent breakable ACL graphs for bounded decoder replay, stable graph input/output addresses, trim-threshold selection and Engram input refresh. It explicitly keeps dynamic EP MoE outside PIECEWISE capture. Therefore a blanket claim that it captures the entire MoE tail or removes every surrounding gap would be incorrect.

Validation should:

1. Verify actual ACL capture/replay of eligible bounded-replay tail segments using #19286, preserving its dynamic EP boundaries.
2. Check correctness across changing replay rows, tail sizes, context lengths, KV state, Engram inputs and DSpark auxiliary outputs; avoid warmup-state specialization.
3. Keep bounded replay, metadata implementation, model, packages, parallelism and workload constant. Compare eager against the graph path at C200/N800, 128K/1K, 90% shared prefix.
4. Compare matched short profiling windows for Host submission and device idle gaps, and measure pure performance separately. Identify remaining dynamic/communication gaps rather than count them as graph-removable.

No fix or end-to-end gain is claimed here. Current timings include profiling overhead, which has not been independently separated from each Host call.

### Other related work

- #21244: batch-level SWA metadata reuse; held constant in the compared captures, distinct from replay-tail graph support.
- #21129: compact SP replay/runtime dispatch; this observed setup uses TP1.

issues.title: [RFC]: KV Cache Pool E2E Watch — PR Gate + Nightly Depth
issues.body:
**TL;DR**

- Add a **test-only** KV Cache Pool E2E watch for vLLM-Ascend.
- **PR**: 12 cases (11 active in the first batch, 1 parked), each ≤15 minutes, parallel jobs.
- **Nightly**: 15 cases, each ≤1 hour, parallel jobs.
- **Delivery**: 4 PRs — PR-A3 (base, shared helpers + 6 A3 cases), PR-A5 (5 A5 cases + routing), Nightly-A3 (9 A3 cases), Nightly-A5 (6 A5 cases). Shared helpers land only in PR-A3; the other three are developed in parallel.
- Shared assertions for startup, accuracy, hit, performance, and SSD; deterministic datasets.
- No runtime behavior changes and no user-facing API changes.

### Motivation.

KV Cache Pool (Ascend Store) is a first-class feature for cross-request and cross-node KV reuse. Current CI coverage is not sufficient:

- PR has only a Qwen3-0.6B connector smoke test: one request, no second load, no external-hit assertion.
- Hybrid linear-attention models (Qwen3.8-27B, GLM-5.3-Flash) keep recurrent Mamba/GDN state outside the block-key, so attention-KV hits alone are not enough; no PR case covers the state copy-after-load path.
- Nightly has no effective pooling watch for most Memcache, Layerwise, PD, CP, PP, and SSD paths.
- Recent field-issue triage (aggregate) shows roughly 47% of KV-pool-related issues involve pooling features; Mooncake, Memcache, and Layerwise are the largest blind spots.
- Pooling failures are often silent: the service starts and requests return, but KV is not written, not read, or read incorrectly.
- Existing cases use 5–40 token prompts, below the 128-token transfer granularity, so they cannot produce a real pool hit.

Without a PR gate and a focused Nightly depth layer, pooling regressions will continue to be found manually after merge.

#### Goals

- PR: 12 cases (11 active; 1 parked), each ≤15 minutes, jobs run in parallel.
- Nightly: 15 cases, each ≤1 hour, jobs run in parallel.
- Shared assertion library: startup, accuracy, hit, performance, SSD, and error-code diagnostics.
- Deterministic datasets: 16K code-constructed prompts for PR; 8-prefix multi-prefix datasets for Nightly.
- CI integration: test routing, estimated times, model/dataset registration, A5 4-card routing.
- Incremental delivery: PR-A3 first (A3 gate unblocked), then PR-A5 and Nightly-A3 in parallel, then Nightly-A5.

#### Non-Goals

- No runtime code changes and no user-facing API changes.
- No >1-hour soak, SSD capacity limit, or full performance matrix.
- No Mooncake SSD offload, CP>1 + Layerwise, GLM-5.3 PP Layerwise, EPLB, or out-of-scope model families.
- No same-case dual-backend pairing.
- No per-case pool-vs-no-pool comparison; we use cold-vs-hit comparison and a self-built performance baseline.

### Proposed Change.

#### 1. How a pool hit happens

1. The scheduler splits the prompt into blocks (block size 128), computes block hashes, and queries the pool.
2. Non-layerwise: the pool query starts after locally computed blocks. Layerwise: the pool is queried from block 0, and the connector returns `max(0, pool_hit - local_hit)`.
3. If matching blocks exist and are not evicted, KV is loaded, then the remaining tokens are prefetched.
4. R1 is the cold write; R2/R3 are the first possible hits; R4 uses a disjoint prompt as the negative check.

A hit requires: prompt length ≥ 2 blocks (16K target), a shared prefix, a completed warmup write, sufficient pool capacity, local prefix cache explicitly disabled, and the same model/tokenizer/parallel topology/block size.

Additional conditions:

- `enable_prefix_caching=False` for hit cases; otherwise local prefix cache can satisfy the request and external-hit metrics become zero.
- `disable_log_stats=False` when using `get_metrics()`.
- The warmup save must be visible before R2/R3; async save does not require a fixed sleep, but the case must not issue the hit request before the write is visible.
- PD: the D side keeps `consumer_is_to_load=false`; pool hit is asserted on the P side, and D receives KV through PD transfer.
- DSV4.1 cases set `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`.
- For spec decode (`use_eagle`), the last lcm block is trimmed. A 16K prompt aligned to the lcm boundary can produce 0 hits; 16388 can hit 16384; 32K can hit 16384. Spec-decode cases use exact hit-token expectations, not the 0.9 ratio.
- Hybrid linear-attention models (e.g. Qwen3.8-27B, GLM-5.3-Flash) require `mamba_cache_mode="align"`, which requires prefix caching. These hit cases therefore keep `enable_prefix_caching=True` and call `LLM.reset_prefix_cache(reset_connector=False)` between rounds: local KV is dropped, pool content is kept, and external hits stay observable. Hybrid prompts use `lcm_block_size + 4`, with `lcm_block_size` read from the pool worker log.
- Hybrid non-Layerwise pooling must set `load_async=false`; otherwise the Mamba state copy after load is skipped and the output is silently wrong.
- GLM-5.3-Flash RecoverSSM requires `mamba_cache_mode="none"` and prefix caching disabled, which is incompatible with pooling; the PR case sets `use_replayssm=False`.

#### 2. Assertion model

| Layer | Assertion | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| S | Service starts; available KV memory satisfies `max_model_len` | Catch startup/OOM regressions |
| A1 | R1 cold output == R2/R3 hit output, token by token | Verify loaded KV is consistent |
| A2 | Output is non-empty, length is sane, no degenerate repetition, expected prefix/format | Lightweight sanity |
| A3 | 8–16 constructed QA prompts with deterministic answers, only on 1–2 representative cases | Optional model-level accuracy |
| H1 | `Δhits > 0` | Pool is actually used |
| H2 | `Δhits / Δqueries ≥ expected_hit_ratio × 0.9` | Pool is useful; non-spec only |
| H3 | Hit-round output == cold-round output | Hit-layer content gate; shares the A1 comparison |
| P | TTFT P50/P95 and input token throughput vs a 10-run baseline, ±5% on the worse side | Performance regression |
| SSD | `capacity > 0`, `status = 0`, `get_hits_ssd > 0`; Nightly also checks `evict/rewarm` | SSD tier is actually used |
| L4 | Scan known pool error signatures; diagnostic first, blocking later | Transport and device errors |

A1 and H3 share the same comparison; A1 reports it as an accuracy check, H3 reports it as a hit-layer gate. No separate no-pool engine is started.

Performance baseline:

- 10 identical runs in a stable environment; record mean, min, and max.
- A baseline with `(max-min)/mean > 5%` is not eligible for gating.
- PR runs one measurement; if it is outside the baseline, retry up to two times and use the median of three.
- Baseline files include an environment fingerprint: image digest, driver, commit, model, dataset hash, concurrency.
- TPOT is not a pooling-watch metric.

#### 3. PR cases (12; 11 active + 1 parked)

| # | Case | Model | Platform | Backend / mode | Topology | Target load | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `four_card/test_deepseek_v4.py` | DeepSeek-V4-Flash | A3 | Mooncake block-key Layerwise | 4-card, TP4 | 16K × 4 | Existing, modify |

Nightly counts:

- 15 total = Memcache 11 + Mooncake 4.
- Platform distribution: A3 9, A5 6 (#4 GVA 4-card, #5 SSD 8-card, #10 performance 4-card, #11 N9 4-card, #14 GLM-5.3-Flash 8-card, #15 Qwen3.8-27B 4-card).
- N8 is removed because it duplicates PR #2.
- 15 is conditional on the shortened GLM-5.3 PP, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, W1, and W2 cases fitting within 1 hour. If any shortened case cannot fit, its full version moves to the future long-run layer and the Nightly count decreases accordingly.
- #10 is a performance run. If PR #9 stays on A5, #10 provides a longer baseline; if PR #9 exceeds the 15-minute budget it moves to Nightly instead of falling back to DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4, and #10 remains the only Nightly A5 performance case.
- Delivery split: **Nightly-A3** carries #1/#2/#3/#6/#7/#8/#9/#12/#13 (9 cases); **Nightly-A5** carries #4/#5/#10/#11/#14/#15 (6 cases).

#### 5. Coverage matrix

| Path | PR | Nightly |
|---|---|---|
| Non-Layerwise basic save/load | DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash A5 4-card, Qwen3.8-27B TP2, GLM-5.3-Flash dummy TP4 | PD-MRV2, GLM-5.3-Flash PD, GLM-5.3-Flash A5, GLM-5.3 PP shortened, A5, DSpark-PCP, Qwen3.8-27B A3/A5, N9, W1/W2 shortened |
| GVA Layerwise | — | DeepSeek-V4-Flash A5 |
| Block-key Layerwise | DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4 | DeepSeek-V4-Flash A3 |
| PD + non-Layerwise | — | PD-MRV2, GLM-5.3-Flash PD, GLM-5.3 PP shortened, W1/W2 shortened |
| CP>1 | DeepSeek-V4-Flash CP2 | DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash P CP4, DSpark-PCP, W1 P CP4 |
| TP mismatch | — | GLM-5.3-Flash P-side reuse |
| PP | DeepSeek-V4-Flash PP2 (parked), Qwen3.8-27B PP2×TP2 (#11) | GLM-5.3 PP shortened |
| DP | DeepSeek-V4-Flash DP2 | A5 DP8 |
| Spec decode / MTP / DSpark | DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash PR two cases, DeepSeek-V4-Flash DP2, Qwen3.8-27B #11 (MTP) | DSpark-PCP, Qwen3.8-27B MTP |
| Hybrid Mamba/GDN | Qwen3.8-27B #10 (non-spec), #11 (PP + MTP); GLM-5.3-Flash #12 (dummy) | Qwen3.8-27B A3 + A5 |
| SSD tier | DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash A5 standalone hit (#8); #3/#6 pilots (#2 is DRAM-only) | A5 hit + small eviction |
| HIXL/PD | — | W1/W2 shortened (platform UB/TLS required) |

Known gaps (not in this RFC):

- Mooncake SSD offload.
- CP>1 + Layerwise.
- GLM-5.3 PP Layerwise.
- GLM-5.3-Flash RecoverSSM + pooling (RecoverSSM requires `mamba_cache_mode="none"` and no prefix caching).
- EPLB, long-run soak, SSD capacity limit, and full performance matrix.
- Out-of-scope model families.

#### 6. Harness and repository changes

Only test and CI files are touched:

- `tests/e2e/pull_request/kv_pool_watch.py` (new): H1/H2/H3, A1/A2, R4 negative check, snapshot deltas, error-code scan; plus a local-cache-reset variant for hybrid models.
- `tests/e2e/conftest.py`: `VllmRunner.get_metrics()` and `DPVllmRunner.get_metrics()`.
- `tests/e2e/common/kv_pool/config.py`: pool config and metrics ports.
- `tests/e2e/common/single_node/kv_pool_runtime.py`: Memcache/Mooncake lifecycle, standalone, loop-backed SSD.
- `tests/e2e/common/single_node/pool_watch.py`: hit/SSD watch handler.
- New or modified PR test files listed above, including `two_card/pool/test_qwen38_mamba_pool.py`, the Qwen3.8-27B PP+MTP case, and the GLM-5.3-Flash dummy-weight pool test.
- New Nightly YAMLs and `nightly_config.yaml` registration.
- `.github/workflows/scripts/test_config.yaml`, `estimated_times.yaml`.
- `.github/workflows/misc/model_dataset_list.json`.

File ownership across the 4 PRs:

- **PR-A3 (base)**: `tests/e2e/pull_request/kv_pool_watch.py`, `tests/e2e/conftest.py`, the six active A3 PR test files (#1/#3/#6/#7/#11/#12), and A3 entries in `estimated_times.yaml`. No `test_config.yaml` change.
- **PR-A5**: the five A5 PR test files (#2/#4/#8/#9/#10), `four_card_a5/pool/__init__.py`, `two_card/pool/__init__.py`, `test_config.yaml` (`a5-2` partition, 5 `runner_mapping` rules, 4 `curated_tests.a5` entries), A5 entries in `estimated_times.yaml`, and `models.a5` for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash / Qwen3.8-27B. Runs one A3 pool smoke test as a helper regression guard.
- **Nightly-A3**: A3 Nightly test YAMLs/scripts, shared Nightly runtime (`common/single_node/kv_pool_runtime.py` standalone + loop SSD, `common/single_node/pool_watch.py`), `nightly_config.yaml` A3 section, and A3 `estimated_times.yaml` entries.
- **Nightly-A5**: A5 Nightly test YAMLs/scripts, `nightly_config.yaml` A5 section, A5 `estimated_times.yaml` entries, and GLM-5.3-Flash in `models.a5`.

Shared helpers (`kv_pool_watch.py`, `conftest.py`) are modified only in PR-A3; the other three PRs consume them read-only to avoid semantic conflicts.

No production code path is modified.

#### 7. Dataset strategy

- PR: code-constructed 16K prompts; no dataset file. R1 writes, R2/R3 reuse the same prompt, R4 uses a disjoint prompt.
- Nightly: reuse existing prefix90/100 datasets where available; add multi-prefix datasets with `prefix_num=8`, `repeat_rate=0.9`, block-aligned prefixes, warmup + main.
- Tokenizer and block alignment are validated per model; dataset names include seed/parameters; SHA256 is recorded.
- Datasets are not committed to the repository; runners generate them or fetch them from an external cache.
- Single-prefix repeated is the easiest hit path; multi-prefix is harder and is used to cover multi-key indexing, capacity, and eviction, not as a prerequisite for a hit.

#### 8. CI integration and cost

- `four_card_a5/pool/*` routes to the A5 4-card runner; `two_card/pool/test_qwen38_mamba_pool.py` routes to the A5 2-card runner (`a5-2`) through `runner_mapping`. #10 is not added to `curated_tests.a5` because that job force-overrides the runner label to `a5-4`.
- `four_card_a5/pool/test_pool_ssd_hit.py` routes to the A5 4-card runner (standalone + loop SSD).
- `four_card_a5/pool/test_pool_perf.py` routes to A5; if it exceeds 15 minutes, the performance smoke moves to Nightly instead of falling back to DeepSeek-V4-Flash.
- The four four-card A5 cases are added to `curated_tests.a5`; #10 is excluded (see above).
- `estimated_times.yaml` must include every new case, including the Qwen3.8-27B 2-card case and the modified PP+MTP / GLM-5.3-Flash files; otherwise coverage validation fails.
- `model_dataset_list.json` must register the A5 models (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, Qwen3.8-27B; GLM-5.3-Flash for Nightly); otherwise offline loading fails.
- Nightly cases are registered under the appropriate runner groups.
- Delivery order: PR-A3 → (PR-A5 ∥ Nightly-A3) → Nightly-A5. Only PR-A3 touches shared helpers; A5-only configuration (`a5-2` partition, runner label, `models.a5`) stays out of PR-A3 so the A3 gate is not blocked by A5 infrastructure.
- This work increases runner minutes. Per-case budgets require parallel runners; a single serial runner cannot meet them. Runner quota must be approved before merge.

#### 9. Alternatives considered

- **Keep only the existing connector smoke test**: cheap, but no hit/content assertion; silent corruption remains invisible.
- **Put everything in Nightly**: no PR gate; feedback arrives too late.
- **Keep a full three-layer weekly design**: long-run, capacity, and functional checks are mixed; budgets and ownership are unclear.
- **Run pool-vs-no-pool for every case**: doubles engine startup and increases flakiness; cold-vs-hit plus a self-built performance baseline is cheaper and sufficient.
- **One mega-case covering all paths**: hard to attribute failures and hard to keep within per-case budgets.

#### 10. Risks and mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Test runtime and flakiness | Per-case budgets; parallel jobs; repeat only on out-of-range performance |
| CI runner quota | Approve 4-card, A5-4, 32-card, and 4-node runner groups before merge |
| A5 4-card model load may approach 15 min | Measure first; if performance smoke exceeds 15 min, move #9 to Nightly |
| A5 standalone + SSD hit may exceed 15 min | Reduce main rounds first; otherwise move #8 to Nightly |
| DP2/CP2 + SSD has no precedent | Pilot first; record objective limitations if unsupported |
| Shortened Nightly cases may exceed 1 h | Move the full version to the future long-run layer |
| 10-run baseline may exceed 5% spread | Do not gate until stable; start with record-only |
| Multi-prefix generator not migrated | Treat generator migration as a first-class deliverable |
| Dual-node UB/TLS unavailable | Platform dependency; report and resolve, do not silently downgrade |
| Spec-PP Mooncake put / lcm issue | Keep pooling; park the case; track separately |
| Hybrid Mamba/GDN requires prefix caching | `mamba_cache_mode="align"` is mandatory; reset local KV with `reset_prefix_cache(reset_connector=False)` between rounds |
| PP × Hybrid Mamba × pool has no CI precedent | #10 stays the primary witness; #11 is additive and can fall back to Nightly if it fails |
| MTP prompts aligned to the lcm boundary yield 0 hits | Use `lcm+4` and exact hit-token assertions |
| GLM-5.3-Flash real weights do not fit 4 cards | #12 uses functional dummy weights for the cache-layout/pool path only; real-weight accuracy stays in Nightly |
| GLM-5.3-Flash RecoverSSM is incompatible with pooling | Set `use_replayssm=False`; RecoverSSM pooling remains a known gap |

#### 11. Rollout and success criteria

- Phase 0: pilot A5 2-card and 4-card, 16K hit, loop SSD, multi-prefix generator.
- Phase 1: **PR-A3** (base) — shared helpers + 6 active A3 cases + A3 `estimated_times`; no dependency, merge first.
- Phase 2: **PR-A5** (5 A5 cases + routing) and **Nightly-A3** (9 cases + Nightly runtime) in parallel; both depend on the PR-A3 helpers.
- Phase 3: **Nightly-A5** (6 cases); depends on PR-A3 helpers and the PR-A5 model registration.
- Phase 4: full coverage — PR 12 cases (11 active; spec-PP parked) and Nightly 15 cases.

Success criteria:

- Every PR case stays within 15 minutes; every Nightly case stays within 1 hour on the approved runners.
- Every hit case has `Δqueries > 0` and `Δhits > 0`; no vacuous hit assertion.
- Two consecutive green Nightly runs.
- Flaky rate below 5% over two weeks.
- CI cost stays within the approved runner quota.

### Feedback Period.

Two weeks.

### CC List.

_None._

### Any Other Things.

- This RFC is test-only; it does not change runtime behavior or user-facing APIs.
- The work can be split into: (1) assertion library + PR cases + CI routing; (2) Nightly standalone/SSD/pool_watch + Nightly cases; (3) the parked spec-PP fix separately.
- A feature branch can be used if the multi-week work needs one.

#### Open Questions

1. Is A5 4-card + SSD able to stay within 15 minutes per case?
2. Are DP2×TP2 and CP2 + SSD supported without special handling?
3. Can the shortened GLM-5.3 PP, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, and W1/W2 cases stay within 1 hour?
4. Is the 10-run performance baseline stable enough (≤5% spread) on the CI runners?
5. Who owns the multi-prefix dataset generator and the dataset cache?
6. Should Mooncake SSD offload and CP>1 + Layerwise remain future work?
7. Is the PP × Hybrid Mamba × pool combination supported as-is, or should #11 stay Nightly-only until the first green run?
8. Should a real-weight GLM-5.3-Flash PR case be added once an 8-card runner (950DT TP8) is available?
9. Can GLM-5.3-Flash (A5 8-card TP8) and Qwen3.8-27B (A5 4-card TP2 + MTP) stay within 1 hour per case?
10. Is an A5 2-card runner (`a5-2`) provisioned for PR #10? If not, should it fall back to A3 2-card?

#### Decision Requested

- Approve the test-only scope and the PR/Nightly split.
- Approve the 12/15 case scope and the parked spec-PP case.
- Approve per-case budgets and the runner quota required for parallel execution.
- Approve the dataset strategy and the code-split plan.
- Confirm whether a feature branch is preferred for the multi-week work.

issues.title: [BugFix]fix DeepSeek-V4 PIECEWISE ACLGraph accuracy
issues.body:
## Summary

This PR fixes an accuracy issue for DeepSeek-V4 when running with PIECEWISE ACLGraph mode on Ascend.

DeepSeek-V4 DSA attention uses the Ascend custom op `vllm::dsa_forward`, but PIECEWISE splitting only added `vllm::mla_forward` as an Ascend custom attention boundary. As a result, the DSA attention path was not treated as a split boundary and could be captured inside a regular PIECEWISE graph segment, leading to incorrect outputs.

This change adds `vllm::dsa_forward` to `compilation_config.splitting_ops` together with `vllm::mla_forward`.

## Changes

- Add `vllm::dsa_forward` to PIECEWISE `splitting_ops`.

## Why

`vllm::dsa_forward` wraps the DeepSeek-V4 DSA attention path. It depends on runtime `forward_context` metadata, KV cache state, sparse attention metadata,and mutates the provided `output` tensor.

Because of these dynamic side effects, it must be handled as a PIECEWISE split boundary instead of being captured inside a normal graph segment.

issues.title: [Feature][Model] Replace DeepSeek V4.1 compressor with AscendC
issues.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Replace the DeepSeek V4.1 C2 compressor's FP32 projection and Triton pooling path with the AscendC `CompressorV2` operator. The operator combines KV/gate projections, pooling, and FP32 ring-state updates; the adapter maps compact outputs back to completion-token rows. RMSNorm, RoPE, cache writers, C1, and the original DeepSeek V4 operator remain unchanged.

This ports PR #17282 at `340d0ac9a783d034054623269e3028cec3a9617d` onto main `95753074cb37f6299024937993100de9c8d7000d`. All 35 vendored operator-directory files match the source PR. The port preserves the native bindings, adapter, ring-wrap fix, speculative graph-capture position fix, and regression coverage, with compatibility changes for current hardware profiles, multistream execution, the V1 runner location, MRv2 initialization, and existing attention tests.

In the measurements below, replacing the compressor reduced complete Prefill compressor subgraph kernel time by **28.02%** and improved output throughput by **5.18%–17.65%** across three E2E scenarios. Complete Decode compressor subgraph kernel time increased by **174.46%**, mainly in the output adaptation chain. Both implementations achieved approximately **90% GPQA Diamond accuracy**.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. V4.1 C2 directly uses AscendC; rebuilding custom operators is required. The previous FP32-projection/Triton-pooling production path and opt-in switch are removed. Both wkv and wgate are stored as BF16. Projections accumulate into FP32, and ring state remains FP32. Converting BF16 checkpoint weights to FP32 in the old path did not add weight precision; end-to-end equivalence still needs comparison.

Model integration currently supports A2/A3 and fails explicitly for unsupported hardware/shapes. A5 sources are included, but its 32-row ring integration is not qualified.

### How was this patch tested?

#### Static validation

- Ruff check/format, Python syntax, symbolic Meta, package initialization, and Git diff whitespace checks passed.
- All 35 vendored operator-directory Git blobs match the source PR.
- Full `bash format.sh ci` was attempted but stopped while fetching hook dependencies with proxy HTTP 407.
- NPU build/runtime validation was not performed during the initial port. Subsequent service, profiling, and accuracy measurements are reported below.

#### Legacy Triton coverage restoration (eeac4fce5)

- Restored the original FP32 reference and model-entry/scheduling tests, selecting A5 for the legacy compressor path. Restored shared-input identity and zero-tolerance assertions and the real `pool_projected` adapter call in the PCP lifecycle test.
- Static AST comparisons against pre-port main `934236001` confirmed all original test names remain in the affected UT files, the FP32 reference is unchanged, and the restored reference/scheduling bodies differ only in A5 route setup. The model-entry assertions and all four original AscendC operator tests are preserved.
- Ruff check/format, Python syntax and offline repository checks passed. Full `bash format.sh ci` remains blocked by proxy HTTP 407. Torch/vLLM unit tests and NPU execution remain unrun locally; this source comparison is not runtime validation.

#### Backend regression coverage (bddab097a)

- Updated compressor, attention/PCP and V1 runner unit tests for A2/A3 AscendC versus A5 Triton, C1/C2 projection dtypes, preparation failures, empty input, adapter contracts, and padded/speculative capture positions.
- Added an A5 numerical test covering prefill/decode transitions, ring wrap, empty input and untouched cache pages. Restricted the Triton fallback to A5.
- Passed: Ruff 0.14.0 check/format, Python syntax parsing, isolated production-class backend-selection smoke checks, package initialization, symbolic Meta, boolean context-manager, logger, long-function and Git whitespace checks.
- Full `bash format.sh ci` stopped while fetching hook dependencies with proxy HTTP 407. The affected pytest suites were not run because this local environment lacks torch/vLLM; A2/A3 and A5 NPU runtime validation remains pending. The isolated smoke checks do not establish NPU correctness, and the earlier benchmark results below were not rerun for this commit.

#### Benchmark setup and E2E results

The baseline and replacement used the same model, datasets, and service parameters:

- **Prefill (P):** DP4/TP2/PCP2, MRV2 and SWA replay enabled, FlashComm disabled.
- **Decode (D):** DP8/TP2, replay disabled.
- Each of the six performance tests was run twice, with no additional retries. The three E2E results are listed below.

Results are calculated from the two-run means. Every change rate is **replacement / baseline − 1**. Lower latency and higher throughput indicate improvement.

| Scenario | Concurrency | TTFT change | TPOT change | Input throughput change | Output throughput change | QPS change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| E2E 128K/1K | 32 | −11.87% | −9.78% | +16.21% | +16.21% | +16.21% |
| E2E 16K/1K | 64 | −19.67% | −9.62% | +17.65% | +17.65% | +17.65% |
| E2E 128K/1K | 64 | −4.20% | −3.32% | +5.18% | +5.18% | +5.18% |

The 128K E2E scenarios had an actual cache hit rate of **89.94%**; input throughput includes cache-hit tokens. The remaining scenarios had a **0%** cache hit rate.

#### Profiling setup and complete-subgraph results

P and D were each profiled five times for both implementations: **20 valid windows and 320 rank-level records**, with every window shorter than two seconds. Both services used the same request: **131,076 input tokens, 4,096 output tokens, and concurrency 1**. The comparison covers complete compressor invocations after computation reached a steady state.

| Stage | Baseline, mean ± standard deviation | Replacement, mean ± standard deviation | Kernel-time change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Prefill | 1514.49 ± 1.76 μs | 1090.18 ± 24.39 μs | −28.02% |
| Decode | 54.98 ± 0.08 μs | 150.90 ± 1.29 μs | +174.46% |

The metric is the **sum of kernel durations within the complete subgraph**, not elapsed wall-clock time. Each round first averages active ranks with equal weight; the reported statistics then summarize the five rounds. Durations from different ranks are not added together.

All five rounds agreed on direction: Prefill decreased by **25.76%–29.90%**, while Decode increased by **171.81%–177.48%**.

**Prefill:** The complete path showed a consistent local improvement. In the baseline, input Cast took **204.71 μs** and the two FP32 projections together took **1248.92 μs**. In the replacement, Fill/Concat, CompressorV2 itself, and output adaptation took **301.47 μs**, **581.56 μs**, and **207.16 μs**, respectively. The complete path saved approximately **424.31 μs per invocation**.

CompressorV2 still showed a latency tail: of 60 invocations, 53 averaged approximately **508 μs**, while the other seven averaged approximately **1136 μs**. Those slower invocations coincided with lower Fill/Concat time; the cause remains undetermined.

**Decode:** The main regression was in output adaptation. For the measured **6×5120** input shape, CompressorV2 itself took **48.99 μs**, while output adaptation took **98.52 μs**, or **65.3%** of the complete path. Cumsum alone took approximately **67.85 μs**, exceeding the baseline's complete subgraph; MaskedFill took approximately **16.13 μs**. Optimizing or combining this adaptation chain is the priority for follow-up work.

**Scope of the comparison:** The local Decode regression and E2E improvement coexist. Profiling measures local kernel costs for a specific shape at concurrency 1, whereas the performance tests measure complete serving behavior at concurrency 32/64. These metrics cannot be directly converted into one another, and the measurements do not establish that any single local change explains the full throughput improvement.

#### GPQA Diamond accuracy

Three GPQA Diamond runs produced:

| Implementation | Accuracy, mean ± standard deviation |
| --- | ---: |
| AscendC replacement | **90.24% ± 1.54%** |
| Original Triton implementation | **90.57% ± 0.29%** |

Both used the same Chat Prompt and evaluation parameters: `temperature=1`, `max_out_len=65536`, `thinking=true`, `reasoning_effort=low`, and maximum concurrency **32**.

issues.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Enable GLM-5.3-Flash mHC sequence-parallel states across PP stages on Model Runner V2. GLM previously rejected SP+PP, while its intermediate-buffer and graph storage paths assumed full token rows.

- Shard embeddings once on the first stage, pass four local mHC states through native MRV2 PP communication, and gather the final hidden output on the last stage.
- Adapt ordinary tensor views in a private ModelState and graph manager, preserving maximum backing capacity, independent capture containers and output addresses.
- Reuse the worker's existing `all_gather_group=None`, Core send retention and wait-before-forward ordering. No custom wire header, worker step state machine or extra normal-path retention lists are added.
- Keep two model-capability-scoped posting failure guards: an active exception retains partially posted buffers/handles until immediate worker exit. Unrelated posting errors retain native exception identity.

The runtime diff touches five existing production files (+380/-39), with no new production file or upstream vLLM patch. Four-state clone/padding stays functional and nonaliasing.

**Separate prerequisite:** the pinned checkpoint/base needs the hybrid KV planner fix tracked in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/18359. It is excluded from this PR and kept as a common prerequisite in the hardware-validation branches.

Implementation, regression tests and review documentation were prepared with OpenAI Codex assistance. A new reviewer without prior conversation context reviewed the complete candidate; its unused ModelState-spec finding was removed and the follow-up was checked. This is source review, not hardware accuracy qualification.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes, experimental GLM-5.3-Flash SP+PP with the existing `enable_flashcomm1` switch. The admitted path requires MRV2, single-node `mp`, DP1, TP>1, PP>1 with nonempty partitions, mHC, BF16, and eager/NONE or `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` graphs. CP, DBO/microbatch slicing, speculative decoding/MTP, LoRA, fine-grained TP, other graph modes and multi-node execution are rejected for this new combination.

The narrow graph/DP envelope makes physical token T derivation equal across stages from the common scheduler message and graph policy; T is never inferred by inverting local rows (e.g. TP8 maps both T=9 and T=16 to two local rows). Existing non-target model-state and graph paths are unchanged.

issues.title: [Feat][Model] Replace DeepSeek V4.1 A5 operator stack with ds41 wheel operators
issues.body:
Swap the DeepSeek V4.1 A5 operator stack to the ds41 wheel operators (cann_ops_transformer.ops.ds41 family), matching the dsnext environment:

- MQSMLA / QLI / QSLI compute and metadata ops route through the packaged_attention dispatcher contracts to the ds41 wheel; the torch schemas and fake implementations are preserved for contract tests.
- Fuse the indexer K pipeline (wk projection + RMSNorm + partial RoPE + MXFP4 quantization + dual-plane cache write) into the single indexer_prologue_k operator (storage_mode=0 separated planes for QLI, storage_mode=1 folded plane for QSLI).
- Replace the ratio-2 compressor with the fused ds41 compressor op (projection + gated pooling inside the op); the eager Triton path is kept as pool_projected_eager for non-A5 devices.
- Quantize the indexer query with npu_dynamic_mx_quant (quantize_query_mxfp4), replacing the Triton quantize_mxfp4_indexer module (removed together with its orphaned cache-write entry point).
- Use the wheel kv_compress_epilog_v2 for A5 KV cache writes.
- Swap mHC to npu_hc_pre_v2 / mhc_post and RMSNorm to npu_rms_norm on A5; non-A5 devices keep the in-tree v3 / npu_hc_post / DeviceOperator paths via _DS41_WHEEL_OPS and uses_a5_packed_cache gating, so environments without the wheels boot and run unchanged.
- Adapt DeepseekV41RMSNorm for the indexer k_norm and compressor norm.
- Walk DeepseekV41Compressor / DeepseekV41Indexer process_weights_after_loading from the top-level model hook to adapt wheel operands after checkpoint loading (local Nz wk conversion, BF16 compressor weights on A5).

Validated on A5: greedy outputs identical to the pre-swap baseline, indexer indices bit-exact, SMLA metadata blobs identical, FULL_DECODE_ONLY + DSpark graph capture clean, GPQA-Diamond 180/198 (90.91%); on A3: in-tree fallback paths run without the wheels.

### What this PR does / why we need it?
Replaces the DeepSeek V4.1 A5 operator stack with the ds41 wheel operators (matching the dsnext environment):

MQSMLA / QLI / QSLI compute and metadata route through the packaged_attention dispatcher contracts to cann_ops_transformer.ops.ds41; torch schemas and fake impls preserved for contract tests.
Fuses the indexer K pipeline (wk projection + RMSNorm + partial RoPE + MXFP4 quantization + dual-plane cache write) into the single indexer_prologue_k operator.
Replaces the ratio-2 compressor with the fused ds41 compressor op; keeps the eager Triton path (pool_projected_eager) for non-A5 devices.
Quantizes the indexer query with npu_dynamic_mx_quant (quantize_query_mxfp4), removing the orphaned Triton quantize_mxfp4_indexer module.
Uses the wheel kv_compress_epilog_v2 for A5 KV cache writes.
Swaps mHC to npu_hc_pre_v2 / mhc_post and RMSNorm to npu_rms_norm on A5; non-A5 devices keep the in-tree v3 / npu_hc_post / DeviceOperator paths via _DS41_WHEEL_OPS + uses_a5_packed_cache gating, so wheel-less environments boot and run unchanged.
Walks DeepseekV41Compressor / DeepseekV41Indexer process_weights_after_loading from the top-level model hook (local Nz wk conversion, BF16 compressor weights on A5).

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?
No

### How was this patch tested?
Boundary-level precision probe vs the pre-swap baseline: greedy outputs identical, indexer indices bit-exact, SMLA metadata blobs identical.
GPQA-Diamond: 180/198 (90.91%).
FULL_DECODE_ONLY + DSpark graph capture clean; memory footprint slightly lower (≈70 more cache blocks per rank).
A3 fallback verified without the wheels.
UTs: 224/224 passed

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: 
  Covered in the adapted UTs: empty-batch early returns in `select_projected` 
  (`max_cache_seq_len == 0`, `query.shape[0] == 0`), pre-quantized query 
  passthrough (no double quantization), CP scenarios exercising prefill/decode/
  dummy/mixed/empty in `test_dsa_v41_cp.py`, and A3 no-wheel fallback boot.

- [ ] **Regression test**: Not applicable — this PR is an operator-stack 
  replacement (feature), not a bug fix.

- [x] **Error / failure path coverage**: 
  Clear error messages with actionable guidance for: missing ds41 wheel on 
  the A5 packed path (`indexer_prologue_k is None` → RuntimeError), fused 
  compressor invoked on non-A5 (`pool_projected` guard), folded-cache 
  geometry mismatch (`candidate_block_size != INDEX_FOLD_ROWS` → ValueError), 
  and wheel import failure on A3 (try/except → graceful fallback).

- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: 
  Tests assert real tensor-level behavior: the CP test verifies scatter 
  ordering and store counts per scenario; the prequantized-query test 
  ensures the quantizer is not invoked twice; the cache test validates 
  fp32 state dtype, ring-pool pointer identity, and norm output. The 
  boundary-level precision probe (36 tagged boundaries, ~180K log lines) 
  confirmed bit-exact indices and metadata blobs against the pre-swap 
  baseline.

- [x] **Performance impact**: 
  Attention/indexer/compressor are performance-critical paths. The fused 
  stack shows slightly lower memory footprint (≈70 more KV cache blocks 
  per rank vs baseline) from replacing 5-step eager chain with single 
  fused ops. Throughput is comparable; JIT compilation overhead of wheel 
  bindings is absorbed by FULL_DECODE_ONLY graph capture at startup.
  No formal benchmark attached; can provide aisbench data if requested.

issues.title: [Feature][Model] Support GLM-5.3-Flash on Ascend 950
issues.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Adapts vllm-ascend for GLM-5.3-Flash (hybrid KDA linear attention + NoPE
sparse MLA, native FP8) on Ascend 950.

The architecture itself now lives in this repository, under
`vllm_ascend/models/glm5next/`, so the PR no longer depends on the unmerged
upstream GLM-5.3-Flash PR (vllm-project/vllm#53906). Every `vllm` symbol the
ported code imports — 139 of them — resolves against vLLM main. What the port
required on the Ascend side is described in *Porting the architecture
downstream* below.

Three defects made the model emit fluent-looking but wrong output, or fail
only in environments other than the author's, so they are worth calling out:

1. `MHCPreOp` / `MHCFusedPostPreOp` accept `norm_weight` / `norm_eps` in
   `forward_native`, but `mhc_pre_torch` has no such parameters. Out-of-tree
   platforms reach `forward_native` through `forward_oot`, so all 45 layers
   ran without their input RMSNorm. No NaNs, plausible activation magnitudes,
   incoherent text.
2. In the chunked-context prefill path, MLA-NoPE leaves both the rope cache
   and its gather output zero-width, and `npu_gather_pa_kv_cache` then returns
   without filling the latent output. Any prompt longer than
   `max_num_batched_tokens` therefore attended over uninitialised KV. GSM8K
   dropped to 0.040.
3. Replacing an op by rebinding its defining module does not reach callers
   that already did a from-import. The GLM vision tower is imported during
   model registration, before `adapt_patch` runs, so it kept the CUDA fused
   Q/K RMSNorm kernel and crashed on `tl.extra.cuda.gdc_wait`. The patch now
   sweeps `sys.modules`.

Full list of defects this PR fixes, each with the symptom that identifies it:

| Symptom | Root cause | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fluent but incoherent text; no NaNs, plausible activations | `mhc_pre_torch` has no `norm_weight` / `norm_eps`, so `forward_native` dropped every layer's input RMSNorm on out-of-tree platforms | `patch/worker/patch_triton.py` |
| Prompts longer than `max_num_batched_tokens` return only `!`; GSM8K 0.040 | rope cache and its gather output are both zero-width, so `npu_gather_pa_kv_cache` leaves the latent output unfilled | `attention/mla_v1.py` |
| Vision tower raises `module 'triton.language.extra.cuda' has no attribute 'gdc_wait'` | the module was imported during model registration, before the patch ran, so its from-import kept the CUDA kernel | `patch/worker/patch_triton.py` |
| FIA rejects `input_layout BNSD_NBSD`; reshape of a 0-element tensor | `qk_rope_head_dim == 0` leaves the rope operands empty and FIA falls back to GQA | `attention/mla_v1.py`, `ops/mla.py`, `ops/rotary_embedding.py` |
| `ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 2)` while loading weights | CANN 9.1 `npu_dynamic_mx_quant` returns `[out, in // 64, 2]`, the MXFP8 method unpacks `[out, in // 32]` | `quantization/methods/w8a8/fp8_block.py` |
| `AssertionError` on `state.is_cuda` in the KDA path | `gather_initial_states` / `scatter_states` are CUDA-only and their kernels reference `gdc_wait` | `patch/worker/patch_triton.py` |
| `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for -: 'NoneType' and 'int'` at scheduler init | the hybrid coordinator receives `num_prefill_lookahead=None` while the non-hybrid path guards it | `patch/platform/patch_kv_cache_coordinator.py` |
| `block_size must be divisible by hash_block_size` | the GLM kpool tail uses `block_size=index_kpool` and opts out of prefix caching | `patch/platform/patch_kv_cache_coordinator.py` |
| `'NoneType' object has no attribute 'decode'` during ACL graph update | hybrid KDA+MLA models register every layer but only MLA layers contribute a captured op | `attention/mla_v1.py`, `worker/model_runner_v1.py` |
| MTP fails to start (four separate interface mismatches) | the spec-decode path assumes a DeepSeek-shaped, text-only target model | `spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py` |
| ACL graph capture aborts with 107027 / stalls at decode-FULL | the 310P `causal_conv1d_update` fallback calls `.item()`, a host sync | `patch/worker/patch_triton.py` |

### Porting the architecture downstream

The model definition, config classes, multimodal processor and MTP module are
carried under `vllm_ascend/models/glm5next/` and registered through
`ModelRegistry.register_model`. Three helpers that upstream satisfies with CUDA
kernels have Ascend equivalents in `vllm_ascend/models/glm5next/ops/`:

| Helper | Upstream | Here |
| --- | --- | --- |
| KDA chunk / recurrent | CUDA Triton in `third_party/flash_linear_attention` | the existing NPU Triton entry points in `vllm_ascend.ops.triton.kda`, imported directly |
| `fwht128_quant_fp8` | fused Hadamard-128 rotation + block-128 ue8m0 FP8 quantization | torch against a cached normalized Hadamard matrix, keeping the bf16 materialization before quantizing; device-side only, so ACL-graph safe |
| `gather_initial_states` / `scatter_states` | Triton kernels asserting `state.is_cuda` | plain `index_select` / `index_copy_`, no host sync |

`causal_conv1d` routes to the Ascend kernels through a local wrapper that drops
the CUDA-side cache-management kwargs once instead of at each call site.

`KpoolTailSpec` / `KpoolTailManager` register through vLLM's
`register_custom_kv_cache_specs` platform hook, which runs after the built-in
specs, so the kpool tail layers keep their own spec without patching the
registry.

Config registration still needs a patch, because the architecture is
downstream: `_CONFIG_REGISTRY` learns the three GLM-5.3-Flash config classes,
and `is_deepseek_mla` is widened because upstream resolves it from a hard-coded
`model_type` whitelist. Both are documented in `vllm_ascend/patch/__init__.py`
with a removal condition.

Two consequences worth calling out:

- The monkey patches that rebound module attributes on
  `vllm.models.glm5next.nvidia.kda` are now unreachable and have been removed.
  The remaining patches in `patch_triton.py` target upstream modules that the
  ported code still goes through (mHC, the vision tower's fused Q/K RMSNorm,
  the mamba state ops, FLA's KDA entry points), so they stay.
- The kpool sparse indexer keeps its `CustomOp` layer so the index-K and tail
  caches still build, but the scoring path raises on Ascend. Upstream
  implements it as fused CUDA kernels (DeepGEMM block-FP8 MQA logits, paged MQA
  logits, radix top-k over a device workspace) with no NPU equivalent yet.
  GLM-5.3-Flash only enables it when a checkpoint sets `index_topk`; the
  configuration validated here is dense NoPE MLA plus KDA.

### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

No new flags. GLM-5.3-Flash requires `--block-size 512`, since the kpool
indexer uses `index_kpool * 32`. Serving no longer requires a vLLM branch
carrying #53906; vLLM main plus this branch is enough.

### How was this patch tested?

Ascend 950PR x8, TP=8, native FP8 checkpoint, `--max-model-len 131072`,
`--block-size 512`, ACLGraph enabled.

Everything below was re-run in a **brand-new container**, with vllm-ascend
installed from this branch as it stood before the port and vLLM pinned to a
fixed commit, to make sure no local state from development was involved.
ACLGraph captured cleanly (piecewise 4/4, decode FULL 4/4 in 20 s) and prefill
reached 6399.8 tokens/s, matching the development environment.

That run therefore resolved the model from a vLLM branch carrying #53906, on
the same checkpoint and the same kernels. The port relocates the model
definition and swaps the three helpers listed above, leaving the dense NoPE
MLA + KDA execution path unchanged, so a re-run on the ported tree is the
remaining thing to confirm.

Accuracy, GSM8K 5-shot via lm-eval `local-chat-completions`, 250 questions,
greedy:

| Configuration | flexible-extract | strict-match |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| before the chunked-gather fix, no MTP | 0.040 | 0.036 |
| after the fix, no MTP | 0.896 | 0.860 |
| after the fix, MTP `num_speculative_tokens=3` | 0.880 | 0.860 |
| after the fix, MTP=5, clean container rebuild | 0.892 | 0.856 |

The first row is the regression signature of defect 2. The last three agree
within one standard error (±0.02).

Correctness of the chunked-context path, as a single deterministic request:
a 28282-token prompt asking for the last number in the text answers `1200`
exactly. Before the fix the same prompt returned only `!` tokens.

AIME2026:

aime26 report table:
┌───────────────┬───────────┬────────────┬──────────┬───────┬─────────┐
│ Model         │ Dataset   │ Metric     │ Subset   │   Num │ Score   │
├───────────────┼───────────┼────────────┼──────────┼───────┼─────────┤
│ glm-5.3-flash │ AIME-2026 │ Accuracy ↑ │ default  │    30 │ 86.7%   │
└───────────────┴───────────┴────────────┴──────────┴───────┴─────────┘ 

gpqa_diamond report table:
┌───────────────┬──────────────┬────────────┬──────────┬───────┬─────────┐
│ Model         │ Dataset      │ Metric     │ Subset   │   Num │ Score   │
├───────────────┼──────────────┼────────────┼──────────┼───────┼─────────┤
│ glm-5.3-flash │ GPQA-Diamond │ Accuracy ↑ │ default  │   198 │ 77.8%   │

Both numbers are lower bounds, in the same direction and for the same reason.
Generations that exhaust the 40960-token budget while still inside the reasoning
phase emit no final answer and score as wrong: 4 of 30 on AIME 2026, 36 of 198 on
GPQA-Diamond. Their reasoning traces are not degenerate — no repetition loops,
still advancing new case analysis at the cut — so this is the model's reasoning
length on hard items, not a generation defect. I kept the cap rather than raising
it, since capping and scoring over-length generations as wrong is the standard
convention; scoring only the completed subset would be selection-biased upward and
is not reported here.

Performance:

- Single request, real prompt, greedy: 55.6 tokens/s, MTP mean acceptance
  length 2.1-3.1.
- 4 concurrent real prompts: acceptance 53% greedy, 30-44% at temperature=1.0
  / top_p=0.95.
- `vllm bench serve`, random dataset, 64K input / 3000 output, 10 requests:
  aggregate prefill 6400 tokens/s, MTP acceptance 46.21%, acceptance length
  2.39. Acceptance on this dataset is a sensitive indicator of chunked-prefill
  correctness: before the fix it was 0%.

Unit test added: `tests/ut/attention/test_mla_nope_chunked_gather.py` covers
defect 2 and asserts the rope-present path is unchanged.

Known dependencies:

  `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` and `Glm5NextMTPModel` are registered from
  this repository, so neither a vLLM fork nor a cherry-pick of #53906 is
  needed.
- ACLGraph needs `causal_conv1d_update_npu`, which is not in vllm-ascend main
  yet. The binding added here is guarded and falls back when the kernel is
  absent, but decode-FULL capture then stalls on a host sync, so the kernel is
  a hard requirement for ACLGraph on KDA models.

issues.title: [RFC]: Hybrid dense/sparse attention routing for GLM-5.3-Flash
issues.body:
### Motivation. GLM-5.3-Flash uses KeyPool-based selection and sparse MLA attention. When a query’s complete causal history fits within the selection budget, all valid historical tokens are selected, making indexer scoring unnecessary. This opportunity also exists inside longer prefills. With an uncached 8K prompt and a 2K selection budget, the first 2K query rows are full-visible while later rows require sparse selection. This RFC proposes request-aware indexer bypass and hybrid dense/sparse attention routing for GLM-5.3-Flash on Ascend. The implementation should establish the benefit of each component independently. Refs #15665. ### Proposed Change. **Before and after** ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph before["Before: all query rows follow the same path"] direction TB B0["All query rows"] --> B1["KeyPool, tail and KV-cache updates"] B1 --> B2["Indexer query / head-weight projections
Scoring + TopK for all rows"] B2 --> B3["SFA for all rows"] B3 --> B4["Attention output"] end subgraph after["Proposed: request-aware hybrid routing"] direction TB A0["All query rows"] --> A1["KeyPool, tail and KV-cache updates
Preserved for all required tokens"] A1 --> A2["Plan query ranges per request"] A2 -->|"Full-visible rows"| A3["Bypass indexer projections, scoring and TopK
Direct causal indices where needed"] A2 -->|"Selective rows"| A4["Indexer query / head-weight projections
Scoring + TopK over complete causal key history"] A3 --> A5{"Dense path supported
and profitable?"} A5 -->|"Yes"| A6["Dense MLA / FIA"] A5 -->|"No"| A7["SFA"] A4 --> A7 A6 --> A8["Restore common output format
and original query order"] A7 --> A8 A8 --> A9["Attention output"] end ``` For an uncached 8K prompt with a 2K selection budget, the proposed plan routes the first 2K query rows through the full-visible branch and the remaining 6K through sparse selection. Each query retains its complete causal key history. Cache maintenance still covers all required tokens. The diagram shows the target hybrid flow. Indexer bypass is first validated with SFA for both branches; dense routing is enabled only when supported and profitable. **1. Plan query ranges** For selection budget `K`, cached context length `C` and current query length `Q`, initially use the conservative full-visible prefix: ```text full_visible_rows = min(Q, max(0, K - C)) ``` Build the plan from trustworthy metadata, preserving request boundaries, causal positions and original query order. Include cached prefixes and speculative positions without introducing device-to-host synchronization. **2. Bypass redundant indexer work** Continue KeyPool construction, compressor-tail updates and cache writes for the complete required input. Skip indexer query projection, head-weight projection, scoring and TopK for full-visible rows. Generate their valid causal indices directly, and run normal selection for the remaining rows. Selection metadata must describe the selected query ranges without truncating their key history. Preserve existing index-buffer conventions and downstream shared-index consumers. First validate this change with the existing SFA consumer to isolate indexer savings. **3. Add hybrid attention routing** Evaluate a compatible dense MLA/FIA path for full-visible rows while retaining SFA for selective rows. Pack eligible ranges where profitable, then restore results to the same output representation and original row order. Admission must account for NoPE geometry, cache format, projection costs, KV gathering or dequantization, workspace and result-restoration overhead. Retain normal SFA when the alternative is unsupported or more expensive. For larger prefills, separately evaluate masked-MHA execution that preserves model-defined sparse selection. Introduce it only after confirming Ascend operator support, bounded workspace and end-to-end benefit. **4. Validate correctness and profitability** Cover selection-budget and pool/tail boundaries, ragged batches, cached-prefix continuation, chunked prefill, speculative positions and transitions between routes. Compare selected-token sets, attention outputs, cache state and end-to-end generation against normal selection and SFA. Include numerical tolerances, complete natural-stop answers, task accuracy and speculative acceptance behavior. Benchmark indexer bypass and attention routing separately. Report indexer latency, attention latency, TTFT, throughput and peak workspace, including all planning and data-movement costs. Use short, 8K and longer inputs with matched cache policies. Determine routing thresholds from Ascend measurements rather than assuming that every full-visible range benefits from dense execution. ### Feedback Period. At least one week. Feedback is requested on query-range ownership, suitable Ascend attention primitives and profitability criteria. ### Any Other Things. The initial target is GLM-5.3-Flash on MRV2. Reuse existing cache, indexer and attention interfaces where practical. No new environment variable is proposed.

issues.body:
### Your current environment

[vllm-a3-crash_20260907_170631.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31910401/vllm-a3-crash_20260907_170631.log)

- vllm-ascend: quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:glm-5.3-flash-a3
- torch / torch_npu: 2.10.0+cpu / 2.10.0.post2
- CANN: 9.1.0 + a vendor custom-opp package (custom_transformer) providing a high-performance TopKV2 kernel
- Driver / firmware: 25.5.1 (V100R001C23SPC006B220)
- Platform: Atlas A3 super pod node, 16 x Ascend910 (8 chips x 2 dies), TP=16 with EP
- Model: GLM-5.3-Flash-w8a8 (public MIT release)

Launch command (paths sanitized):

```bash
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE=AIV
export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=400
# sources a vendor custom-opp package:
#   /usr/local/Ascend/cann-9.1.0/opp/vendors/custom_transformer/bin/set_env.bash

vllm serve /path/to/GLM-5.3-Flash-w8a8 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 16 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --max-model-len 133120 \
  --max-num-seqs 32 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --quantization ascend \
  --safetensors-load-strategy prefetch \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":1,"video":0}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[1,2,4,8,16,32,64,96,128]}'
```

### 🐛 Describe the bug

The service crashed twice with an identical signature — once after ~16h of uptime and once after
~1.7h after restart — so the failure is uptime-independent and deterministic.

Python-side error (identical in both crashes, in MoE token dispatch preprocess):

```text
File "vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/token_dispatcher.py", line 623, in _preprocess
    global_input_tokens_local_experts_indices = torch.repeat_interleave(
RuntimeError: operator():../torch_npu/csrc/aten/common/LocalScalarDenseNpu.cpp:23 NPU function error:
c10_npu::acl::AclrtSynchronizeStreamWithTimeout(copy_stream), error code is 507035
[ERROR] ERR00100 PTA call acl api failed
[Error]: The vector core execution is abnormal.
```

Device-side error:

```text
The error from device(chipId:x, dieId:y), serial number is 1, there is an exception of fftsplus
aivector error, vec error info: 0x470000020d, subErrType:4, errorStr: The VEC instruction parameter is invalid.
An error occurred in the kernel task, retCode=0x31, [vector core exception]
rtStreamSynchronizeWithTimeout execution failed, reason=vector core exception
```

Key observations:

1. All 16 devices failed in the same second with bit-identical vec error info (0x470000020d).
   npu-smi reports Health OK for every device before and after, and the failing task serial number
   is 1/2 on every device. This looks like a deterministic kernel/tiling bug, not a hardware fault.
2. The device exception dump identifies the failing kernel: the dump directory next to each
   exception_info.* file contains only TopKV2_<hash>_high_performance_*_host.o — i.e. the crashing
   kernel is the custom high-performance TopKV2 from the vendor opp package (MoE routing top-k),
   not repeat_interleave itself; repeat_interleave is only where the stream synchronize surfaced
   the error. The dumps also contain full tiling data (64B) and input tensors.
3. The trigger pattern is reproducible: right before both crashes, a burst of 4 concurrent requests
   with ~32K-token prompts arrived (identical traffic replayed both times: Avg prompt throughput
   3276.7 tokens/s, then Running: 2 reqs, Waiting: 2 reqs), and the crash happened during the first
   mixed chunked-prefill + decode forward passes (max_num_batched_tokens=8192).
4. The crash occurred while the acl-graph wrapper executed the step via its eager fallback
   (acl_graph.py fx_run_eagerly), since the mixed-batch shape is not covered by decode-only graphs.
   Additionally, at startup every worker recorded
   "EE1016: Synchronous memory copy failed ... capture mode GLOBAL(0) ... supported only in
   RELAXED mode" during graph capture — pointing at the same op family (synchronous scalar copy
   inside repeat_interleave) being incompatible with GLOBAL capture.

Current workaround / status:

- Temporarily ran with --enforce-eager and reduced limits (--max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 1):
  service was up, no 507035/EE1016 during that run. However, the original crash happened on the
  eager fallback path, so enforce-eager alone may not fully avoid it.
- Next step we plan to try: drop the custom_transformer vendor opp package from the env so TopK
  falls back to the native implementation, and re-run the trigger traffic.
- npu-smi health is OK; we have per-device exception_info dumps (incl. tiling data) and plog
  available if needed.

Questions:

1. Is this a known issue with the custom high-performance TopKV2 kernel under mixed
   chunked-prefill batches?
2. Is there a supported way to force native TopK for this model (instead of removing the whole
   vendor opp package), e.g. an op-priority config?
3. Any fixed version you can point us to?

issues.title: [Performance][Attention] Optimize fused_sparse_attention_overlap kernel on A3
issues.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

The  `fused_sparse_attention_overlap` operator (poolingSFA) uses KV offload, but the current kernel is not fully optimized: the H2D communication takes a long time, communication and computation are not well overlapped, and the hardware resources are not fully utilized.

This PR optimizes the kernel on the arch22 (A3 / ascend910_93) path:

- **Row-partition parallelism**: set `workerCount = GetBlockNum() * 2` so every AIV subcore joins `RunAllCoreSelectionUpdate` (plan=off, bs>24: **-19% ~ -42%** on the selection-update path).
- **Pair-sort**: sort hit pairs by slot number so the paired-copy stride is always positive (copy issue count **-33%**).
- **Writeback path**: skip transposition re-derivation (4 GM scalar reads), read back only tokens actually written, and scan one pair at a time.
- **UB direct write**: flush update entries to the selection cache while data is still in UB; collect-always + full-batch zero-window mask; `directWrittenWindowMask_` lets the writeback path skip windows already handled (hit ratio 0-70%: **+10% ~ +12%**).
- **Windowed two-phase MergeKv main loop** with branch-free batch plan decode (Phase A single-array scheme).
- **Idle-core helper mechanism**: idle cores assist MergeKv via done/credit handshake rings placed in an independent workspace area (`+2*actCoreNum*64*8*4` bytes in tiling); supports plan/LRU paths and update-writeback sharing, gated to full coverage (bs<=12); SyncAll narrowed to helper launches with per-launch handshake zeroing.

All kernel changes are confined to arch22 (A2/A3); the arch35 (Ascend 950) path and the op schema (15 args, no timer) are untouched. The workspace extension in the shared op_host tiling also applies to 950 builds and is harmless there (unused bytes).

**Experiment**
（1 ）**e2e test** Atlas A3，GLM-5.1-w4a8，topk=2048，TP16/EP16，bs=8，prompt=32768，output=1024

| | **after** |   before | delta |

| TPOT med | **145.9 ms**  | 146.9 ms |-0.68%    |
| TPOT mean | **146.5 ms**  | 152.4 ms  |-3.87%    |
| Output throughput | **47.7892 token/s** |46.2626 token/s  | +3.30%  |
| E2EL mean  | **171173.6 ms** |176816.5 ms  | -3.19%    |

（2 ）**kernel test** Atlas A3，GLM-5.1-w4a8，topk=2048，TP16/EP16，bs=4，prompt=65536，output=64

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| fusedSparseAttentionOverlap  | **0.411901 ms** | 0.451008 ms  | -8.67 %   |

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No API, CLI, or configuration change is introduced; the optimized kernels are selected automatically on the existing path.

A release note fragment is required and will be added at `release_notes/fragments/20927.yaml`.

### How was this patch tested?

Tested in the appropriate environment:

```bash
pytest -sv tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/test_fused_sparse_attention_overlap.py
```

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [ ] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: kernel-side edge conditions (bs<=12 helper gating, full-coverage windows, zero-window mask) are exercised by the operator precision suite; no new Python unit tests are added since the change is confined to AscendC kernel sources.
- [ ] **Regression test**: not a bug fix.
- [ ] **Error / failure path coverage**: no new failure paths introduced; handshake rings are zeroed per helper launch.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: operator-level precision validation on A3 asserts real kernel behavior.
- [x] **Performance impact**: benchmark numbers are attached in the description above (row-partition fix: -19% ~ -42%; pair-sort: -33% copy issues; UB direct write: +12%); the optimization applies only to the A3 (arch22) kernel path and is inert on 950.
